sounds.intro: Uzbek is written in the Latin alphabet and is spelled almost exactly as it sounds. There are no genders and no articles. The stress is usually on the last syllable. Learn the special letters first.
rows: a "k" made far back in the throat
notes: In o' and g' the apostrophe is part of the letter. It is not a pause.
Say stands for "how to say it". Capitals mark the stressed syllable.

phrases.title: Formal and informal
phrases.note: sen (informal): friends, family, children. siz (formal): strangers, older people, work. Siz is also "you all". Use siz when unsure.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Uzbek often drops the pronoun, because the verb ending shows who is speaking. Pronouns are for emphasis. There is no he / she difference: "u" means both.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Add -lar to the noun. It is the same for every word, so there is no vowel harmony in the plural. After a number, the noun stays singular: ikki kitob (two book).

grammar.title: To be: -man, -san, -(dir)
text: There is no separate verb "to be". Add an ending to the noun or adjective: talaba-man (I am a student). The ending for "he / she is" is none, or -dir.

grammar.title: Bor and yo'q: have, there is
text: Uzbek says "at me there is" (bor) or "at me there is not" (yo'q). The ending -da means "at" or "in".

grammar.title: Present tense: -yapman
text: The most common present form: verb stem + -yap + person ending. Bormoq (to go): bor-yap-man. After a consonant it is -ayap, e.g. o'qimoq: o'qiyapman.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The verb goes last. Order: who, where or when, what, verb. Uzbek has no articles: "kitob" means "a book" or "the book".

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put -ma- after the verb stem: boraman (I go), bormayman (I do not go). For nouns use "emas" (is not): u o'qituvchi emas. "Yo'q" means "there is not". Always compare with the positive form.
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Add the little word -mi to the end of the sentence. It is the same for every word. Say it with rising voice.

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words stand where the answer would stand.

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: Endings go on the noun: -im (my), -ing (your), -i (his / her). After a vowel: -m, -ng, -si. To say you like something, use "menga yoqadi" (to me it is pleasing).

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: sen (informal): friends, family, children. siz (formal): strangers, older people, work. Verb endings change: -san (informal), -siz (formal).

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: -di + person ending (bordim = I went). Future: -aman is the same as the present, with a time word: ertaga boraman (tomorrow I go).

grammar.title: Commands
text: Use the bare verb stem for informal and add -ing for formal: kel (come), keling (come, formal). For "do not" add -ma: kelma.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: Can: verb + -a olmoq (borolaman, I can go). Must: "kerak" (needed). Want: -moqchi + person ending (bormoqchiman, I want to go).
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Uzbek uses endings, not words in front: -da (in, on, at), -ga (to), -dan (from), -ning (of).
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Add -roq to the adjective for "more": katta, kattaroq. For "the most" put "eng" before it: eng katta. "Than" is -dan.
